new.s: The Girnar rock, which bears Ashoka's 14 Major Rock Edicts, also carries the inscription of which later ruler?
new.x: The same rock at Girnar (Junagadh, Gujarat) that bears Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts later received Rudradaman's inscription.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Girnar rock also bears Rudradaman's inscription

new.s: In which district of Gujarat is Girnar, the site of Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts?
new.x: Girnar, with all 14 Major Rock Edicts, is in Junagadh district of Gujarat.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Girnar -> Junagadh

new.s: In which district of Odisha is the Ashokan edict site of Jaugada?
new.x: Jaugada, with Major Rock Edicts and the Separate Kalinga Edicts, is in Ganjam district of Odisha.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Jaugada -> Ganjam

new.s: Which Major Rock Edict of Ashoka says that Dhammayatras replaced the royal pleasure tours?
new.x: Rock Edict VIII records that Dhammayatras replaced pleasure tours; the first was to Bodh Gaya.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: RE VIII -> Dhammayatras

new.s: In which edicts does Ashoka declare 'All men are my children'?
new.x: The Separate Kalinga Edicts at Dhauli and Jaugada, addressed to the officers of Tosali and Samapa, say 'all men are my children'.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Separate Kalinga Edicts -> 'all men are my children'

new.s: Where are Ashoka's Separate Kalinga Edicts found?
new.x: The Separate Kalinga Edicts are at Dhauli and Jaugada in Odisha, where they replace Rock Edicts XI-XIII.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Separate Kalinga Edicts -> Dhauli and Jaugada

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Ashoka after the Kalinga War:
1. Bherighosha (the sound of war drums) gave way to Dhammaghosha.
2. He gave up wars of conquest.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: After Kalinga, Ashoka gave up wars of conquest and Bherighosha was replaced by Dhammaghosha.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Bherighosha -> Dhammaghosha

new.s: Who among the following carried a branch of the Bodhi tree to Sri Lanka?
new.x: Ashoka's daughter Sanghamitta went to Sri Lanka after Mahinda, taking a branch of the Bodhi tree.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Sanghamitta -> Bodhi tree branch to Sri Lanka

new.s: Which king of Sri Lanka received the Buddhist mission of Ashoka's son Mahinda?
new.x: Mahinda's mission to Sri Lanka was received by king Devanampiya Tissa.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Mahinda -> king Devanampiya Tissa

new.s: To which region were Sona and Uttara sent as Buddhist missionaries after the Third Buddhist Council?
new.x: Sona and Uttara went to Suvarnabhumi (Myanmar/Thailand).
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Sona and Uttara -> Suvarnabhumi

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Missionary) - List-II (Region)
A. Mahadeva - 1. Yona (Greek) country
B. Rakkhita - 2. Mahisamandala
C. Maharakkhita - 3. Himalayan region
D. Majjhima - 4. Vanavasi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: Mahadeva went to Mahisamandala, Rakkhita to Vanavasi, Maharakkhita to the Yona country and Majjhima to the Himalayan region.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: missions -> region (Mahadeva, Rakkhita, Maharakkhita, Majjhima)

new.s: At which of the following places is Ashoka's Schism Edict found?
new.x: The Schism Edict, expelling dissenting monks and nuns, is found at Sarnath, Sanchi and Kaushambi.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Schism Edict -> Sarnath, Sanchi, Kaushambi

new.s: Which Ashokan pillar inscription in Nepal records the enlargement of the Kanakamuni stupa?
new.x: The Nigali Sagar pillar in Nepal records that Ashoka enlarged the Kanakamuni stupa in his 14th year.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Nigali Sagar -> Kanakamuni stupa

new.s: According to Ashoka's Pillar Edict VII, how does Dhamma spread best?
o: By persuasion rather than by law
By the conquest of neighbouring kingdoms
new.x: Pillar Edict VII (only on the Delhi-Topra pillar) says Dhamma spreads better by persuasion than by law.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: PE VII -> persuasion over law

new.s: Which edict of Ashoka recommends Buddhist texts and proves that he was a Buddhist?
new.x: In the Bhabru (Bairat) edict Ashoka states his faith in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha and recommends Buddhist texts.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Bhabru -> Buddhist texts, proves Ashoka Buddhist

new.s: In which district of Karnataka is the Maski Minor Rock Edict of Ashoka?
new.x: Maski, the Minor Rock Edict that names Ashoka, is in Raichur district of Karnataka.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Maski -> Raichur

new.s: Besides Ashoka's edicts and Samudragupta's prashasti, the inscription of which Mughal emperor is found on the Allahabad pillar?
new.x: Jahangir added his inscription to the Allahabad (Kosam) pillar, which had been moved to the Allahabad fort.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Allahabad pillar -> Jahangir's inscription

new.s: By which name is Ashoka called in the Maski edict?
new.x: The Maski edict calls him 'Buddhashakya Ashoka'; Dharmasoka is from Sarnath, Piyadasi Raja from Bhabru and Ashok Vardhan from the Puranas.
new.angle: U0037 notes gap: Maski -> Buddhashakya

new.s: Which edicts of Ashoka are inscribed on the Lauriya Nandangarh pillar?
new.x: The Lauriya Nandangarh pillar bears Pillar Edicts I-VI in Brahmi script; PE VII is found only on the Delhi-Topra pillar.
new.angle: U0037 web fact: Lauriya Nandangarh -> PE I-VI

new.s: In which district of Bihar is the Lauriya Nandangarh pillar of Ashoka?
new.x: The Lauriya Nandangarh pillar, with a single lion capital and Pillar Edicts I-VI, is in West Champaran district of Bihar.
new.angle: U0037 web fact: Lauriya Nandangarh -> West Champaran

new.s: Which was the capital of the Mauryan province of Uttarapatha?
new.x: Taxila was the capital of Uttarapatha; Ujjain of Avantipatha, Suvarnagiri of Dakshinapatha and Tosali of Kalinga.
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: Uttarapatha -> Taxila

new.s: How many provinces did the Mauryan empire have under Chandragupta Maurya?
new.x: There were four provinces under Chandragupta; Kalinga (Tosali) was added later by Ashoka.
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: four provinces under Chandragupta

new.s: Who headed the municipal administration of a Mauryan city?
new.x: A Mauryan city was run by a municipality under the Nagaraka (Purmukhya).
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: Nagaraka -> city head

new.s: Which Mauryan courts, meaning 'removal of thorns', tried criminal cases?
new.x: Kantakashodhana courts tried criminal cases under three pradeshtris; Dharmasthiya courts tried civil cases.
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: Kantakashodhana -> criminal courts

new.s: According to Megasthenes, how many foot soldiers did Chandragupta Maurya's army have?
new.x: Megasthenes gives Chandragupta's army as 6,00,000 foot soldiers and 30,000 cavalry.
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: Chandragupta's army -> 6,00,000 foot

new.s: Among Kautilya's tirthas, what was the Karmantika in charge of?
new.x: The Karmantika was the tirtha in charge of factories and mines.
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: Karmantika -> factories and mines

new.s: Kautilya's saying 'a chariot cannot move on one wheel' stresses the king's need for what?
new.x: Kautilya meant that the king cannot rule alone and needs ministers (the Mantriparishad), a check on his power.
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: 'chariot cannot move on one wheel' -> ministers

new.s: Who was the chief district administrator in the Mauryan empire, in charge of revenue and police?
new.x: The Pradeshika was the chief district administrator, handling revenue and police and touring every five years (RE III).
new.angle: U0038 notes gap: Pradeshika -> chief district administrator

new.s: Who is the author of Indica?
new.x: Megasthenes, the Greek envoy of Seleucus at Chandragupta's court, wrote Indica in Greek.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: Indica -> Megasthenes

new.s: With which work is Kautilya's Arthashastra often compared?
new.x: The Arthashastra, on polity and wealth, is compared with Machiavelli's The Prince.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: Arthashastra ~ The Prince

new.s: Which Chinese pilgrim of the 5th century CE admired the Mauryan palace at Pataliputra?
new.x: Fa-Hien (5th c. CE) admired the palace at Pataliputra; Megasthenes compared it to Susa and Ecbatana.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: Fa-Hien admired Pataliputra palace

new.s: At which places are the Dharmarajika stupas found?
new.x: The Dharmarajika stupas are at Sarnath and Taxila.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: Dharmarajika -> Sarnath and Taxila

new.s: Which of the following caves is on the Barabar hill?
new.x: The Barabar hill has four caves: Lomas Rishi, Sudama, Viswamitra and Karna Chopar; Gopika, Vahiyaka and Vadathika are Nagarjuni caves.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: Barabar hill caves -> Sudama, Lomas Rishi

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan society:
1. The Arthashastra allowed widow remarriage.
2. Shudras could own land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Widow remarriage was allowed in the Arthashastra, and Shudras could own land.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: widow remarriage; Shudras owned land

new.s: Which two types of philosophers did Megasthenes describe in India?
new.x: Megasthenes divided philosophers into Brahmins and Shramanas.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: Megasthenes -> Brahmins and Shramanas

new.s: To which age do the punch-marked silver coins of India go back?
new.x: Punch-marked silver coins, with symbols and no portraits, go back to the Mahajanapada age (6th c. BCE).
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: punch-marked coins -> Mahajanapada age

new.s: In which district of Madhya Pradesh is the Sanchi stupa?
new.x: Sanchi (Kaknam) is in Raisen district, MP, west of the Betwa; Bharhut is in Satna.
new.angle: U0039 notes gap: Sanchi -> Raisen

new.s: The Milindapanha is a dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander and which Buddhist monk?
new.x: Menander (Milinda), whose capital was Sagala, held a dialogue with the monk Nagasena, recorded in the Milindapanha.
new.angle: U0040 notes gap: Milindapanha -> Nagasena

new.s: Which historian blamed Ashoka's pacifism for the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
new.x: H.C. Raychaudhuri held that Ashoka's non-violence after Kalinga weakened the army.
new.angle: U0040 notes gap: Ashoka's pacifism -> Raychaudhuri

new.s: In which Buddhist text is the story of Bavari sending sixteen disciples to the Buddha found?
new.x: Bavari's story is in the Parayana-vagga of the Suttanipata, not in the Jatakas.
new.angle: U0041 notes gap: Bavari -> Suttanipata

new.s: By which writer is Megasthenes' report of the Andhra king's army preserved?
new.x: Megasthenes' report of 1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry and 1,000 elephants of the Andhra king is preserved by Pliny.
new.angle: U0041 notes gap: Megasthenes' Andhra report -> Pliny

new.s: At which place in Andhra Pradesh was a fragment of an Ashokan pillar edict found?
new.x: Amaravati has a fragment of an Ashokan pillar edict; Erragudi and Rajula Mandagiri have rock edicts.
new.angle: U0041 notes gap: Amaravati -> Ashokan pillar fragment

new.s: Dhanyakataka (Amaravati-Dharanikota) was the capital of which dynasty in its later phase?
new.x: Dhanyakataka, a Mahasanghika Buddhist centre, was the capital of the later Satavahanas.
new.angle: U0041 notes gap: Dhanyakataka -> later Satavahana capital

new.s: Which early historic site in the Nellore region was declared a Monument of National Importance in July 2026?
new.x: Gottiprolu, a walled trade centre of the 2nd-1st c. BCE excavated by the ASI, was declared a Monument of National Importance in July 2026.
new.angle: U0041 notes gap: Gottiprolu -> Monument of National Importance

new.s: Where is the Heliodorus (Garuda) pillar located?
new.x: Heliodorus set up the Garuda-dhvaja to Vasudeva at Besnagar (Bhilsa/Vidisha) in Madhya Pradesh.
new.angle: U0042 notes gap: Heliodorus pillar -> Besnagar

new.s: Which was the first play of Kalidasa?
new.x: Malavikagnimitram, the love story of Agnimitra and Malavika in 5 acts, was Kalidasa's first play.
new.angle: U0042 notes gap: Kalidasa's first play -> Malavikagnimitram

new.s: Who overthrew Susharman, the last Kanva ruler?
new.x: Simuka, founder of the Satavahana dynasty, overthrew Susharman and ended the Kanva dynasty.
new.angle: U0042 notes gap: Susharman -> overthrown by Simuka

new.s: Which ruler is called Sarvakshatrantaka in the Puranas?
new.x: The Puranas call Mahapadma Nanda (Ugrasen) Sarvakshatrantaka and Aparoparashurama.
new.angle: U0042 notes gap: Mahapadma Nanda -> Sarvakshatrantaka

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Founder) - List-II (Dynasty)
A. Gopala - 1. Kadamba
B. Pravarasena I - 2. Paramara
C. Siyaka II - 3. Pala
D. Mayurasharman - 4. Vakataka
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: Gopala founded the Palas, Pravarasena I the Vakatakas (actual founder), Siyaka II the Paramaras and Mayurasharman the Kadambas.
new.angle: U0042 notes gap: founders -> dynasty (Gopala, Pravarasena I, Siyaka II, Mayurasharman)
